newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Saudi's Alujain to sign MTBE contract in mid-1997.
newsitem.headline: Saudi's Alujain to sign MTBE contract in mid-1997.

text.p: Private Saudi Arabian firm Alujain Corp said on Monday construction of a 850,000 tonnes a year MTBE plant is expected to start in the middle of 1997.
"We expect to sign the plant's construction deal at the end of the first half of 1997," a company official told Reuters.
The plant, which Alujain will build in Yanbu on the Red Sea to produce the environmentally-friendly fuel additive methyul tertiary butyl ether (MTBE), is due to come on stream in 1999.
The official said a new 525 million riyals ($140 million) company, Tahseen, has been formed to run the plant.
Finnish energy group Neste Oy had signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Alujain to become a minority shareholder in the company operating the plant.
Alujain will seek a 400 million riyal loan from the Saudi Industrial Development Fund (SIDF) to partly finance the project, the official said.
Three international firms are bidding for the main project works.
Alujain has declined comment on how much the project would cost, but studies of Alujain's original plan to build a 500,000 tonnes a year MTBE plant showed it would cost $500 million.
